questions.question: According to Annex 2A, paragraph 1.2, which part of the ATMP lifecycle does GMP apply to?

options.A: Only the commercial manufacturing stage after a marketing authorisation (MA) is obtained; investigational products are outside the scope
options.B: From the manufacture of investigational products through to commercial manufacturing; management after product discontinuation is outside the scope
options.C: From investigational ATMP manufacture, technology transfer and commercial manufacture through to product discontinuation
options.D: Only Phase III clinical trials and commercial manufacturing; early clinical stages need only follow development quality principles

questions.explanation: Paragraph 1.2 explicitly states that GMP covers investigational ATMP manufacture, technology transfer and commercial manufacture, up to product discontinuation. Limiting the scope to the commercial stage, or to Phase III and later, does not match the text.

questions.question: An ATMP uses a closed system, and it can be demonstrated that the system remains integral throughout its period of use. According to Annex 2A, paragraph 3.13, what is the lowest acceptable background environment?

options.A: Grade B background, because a closed system must still maintain the same environmental grade as open operations
options.B: Grade C background, the lowest grade a closed system may never go below under any circumstances
options.C: Grade A background, because a closed system may not have its environmental grade requirement reduced on the basis of a QRM assessment
options.D: Grade D background, provided it can be demonstrated that the closed system remains integral throughout its period of use

questions.explanation: Paragraph 3.13, item b, states that if a closed system can be shown to remain integral throughout, a Grade D background can be accepted. The Grade C in 3.13, item a, applies to cases such as single-use sterile assemblies that require appropriate controls, and is not a lower limit.

questions.question: A process is not closed: the product is exposed to the room environment when media and buffers are added, and there is no subsequent microbial inactivation step. According to paragraph 3.11, what environment should be used for aseptic manipulation?

options.A: Grade A with a Grade B background (per Annex 1)
options.B: Grade B with a Grade C background (per Annex 1)
options.C: Grade A with a Grade C background (per Annex 1)
options.D: Grade C with a Grade D background (per Annex 1)

questions.explanation: Paragraph 3.11 requires aseptic manipulations in which the product is exposed to the room environment to be performed in Grade A with a Grade B background, per Annex 1. The other combinations are lower grades and do not match the text.

questions.question: Unless otherwise specified in the MA/CTA or national legislation, how long, according to paragraph 4.7, must traceability records for cell and tissue based products and any personalised ATMP be kept after the expiry date of the product?

options.A: 10 years after expiry, consistent with the retention period for ordinary batch records, after which they may be destroyed
options.B: 30 years after expiry, with attention to donor-matched traceability
options.C: 5 years after expiry, aligned with the retention sample storage period to allow spot checks, after which they may be destroyed
options.D: 15 years after expiry, covering the expected patient follow-up treatment period, after which they may be destroyed

questions.explanation: Paragraph 4.7 requires traceability records to be kept for 30 years after the expiry date. There is no basis in the text for 10, 5 or 15 years, which are easily confused with ordinary record retention periods.

questions.question: Several isolators handling different viral vectors are used at the same time in one room. According to paragraph 3.2, item b, besides closed, segregated and unidirectional flow, what else is required?

options.A: Room air may be partially recirculated, provided the recirculated air is HEPA filtered and monitored monthly
options.B: The room must be kept under negative pressure, and each isolator must use its own dedicated air handling unit
options.C: The room and facility must have 100% air exhaust (no recirculation)
options.D: Only one isolator in the room may be open at any one time, and the others must be completely shut down

questions.explanation: Paragraph 3.2, item b, requires that when several isolators handling different viral vectors are in the same room, the room and facility must have 100% air exhaust with no recirculation. Statements allowing partial recirculation are the opposite of the text.

questions.topic: Returning containers to cell bank stock
questions.question: After a container of a cell bank has been removed from the management system, how should it be handled according to paragraph 5.38?

options.A: If it still carries its original labelling and its temperature has not been exceeded, it may be returned to the original stock with quality unit approval
options.B: As long as visual inspection confirms the container is intact, it may be returned to the same storage location and kept there
options.C: It should be returned to a backup stock location, but must be relabelled and the number of removals noted on the stock list
options.D: It should not be returned to stock, because the storage and handling conditions of the stock must be controlled under a single procedure

questions.explanation: Paragraph 5.38 states that once a container has left the seed lot / cell bank management system, it should not be returned to stock. The other options sound reasonable, but the text does not permit return under any conditions.

questions.question: For an autologous ATMP it is not possible to keep a retention sample of a full packaged unit from every batch. According to paragraph 6.7, what is the reasonable approach?

options.A: Retention is generally not expected; where it cannot be kept, a photograph or copy of the label can be included in the batch record
options.B: A full packaged unit must still be kept until one year after expiry, and a batch for which this is impossible may not be released
options.C: Keep a complete frozen sample of the patient's cells instead, for at least two years before it may be destroyed
options.D: The MAH keeps a reference sample from the same batch instead, which waives all batch record documentation

questions.explanation: Paragraph 6.7 notes that the unit of an autologous product is itself the product to be administered to the patient, so a retention sample is generally not expected; where it cannot be kept, a photograph or copy of the label can be included in the batch record. The statement that a full packaged unit must still be kept and that batches without one may not be released is the opposite of the text.

questions.question: An ATMP is manufactured in a decentralised manner, with a responsible site overseeing the individual locations. According to paragraph 6.16, item b, who bears final responsibility for batch certification, a responsibility that cannot be delegated?

options.A: The person in charge at each decentralised location, because that person knows best the local manufacturing situation and the details of personnel operations
options.B: The Authorised Person of the responsible site (who may rely on data from qualified personnel)
options.C: The clinical trial Sponsor, because it is responsible for overall clinical supply decisions and patient safety
options.D: An inspector appointed by the competent authority, who must review and sign off approval before each batch is released

questions.explanation: Paragraph 6.16, item b, states that the Authorised Person has final responsibility for batch certification, which cannot be delegated, but may rely on information passed on by qualified and trained personnel at the decentralised locations. The other roles are not the responsible persons named in the text.

questions.question: To test the robustness of the recall procedure (or the procedure for notifying healthcare professionals) for ATMPs, what mock recall frequency does paragraph 8.3 recommend for authorised products?

options.A: Once a quarter, and it must be carried out during working hours to ensure staff from all departments are present
options.B: Once every two years, and only the written procedure needs to be exercised, without testing the contact process
options.C: Once a year, unless otherwise justified; and it should cover both working-hours and out-of-hours scenarios
options.D: Once at each product change, with no need to set the frequency according to the stage of product development

questions.explanation: Paragraph 8.3 recommends a mock recall once a year for authorised products unless otherwise justified, and the exercise should cover both working and out-of-hours periods. An option that exercises working hours only would miss the scenarios required by 8.3.

questions.question: For cells, tissues and organs used to manufacture xenogeneic cell based medicinal products, what does Part B, paragraph B 1.5 require of the source animals?

options.A: Only animals housed for this purpose in a barrier facility; wild or abattoir sources are prohibited
options.B: They may come from quarantined wild animals, provided they are handled at an abattoir to food safety standards before use
options.C: They may come from tissues of founder animals, because their genetic background is the best defined and their health records are complete
options.D: They may come from any healthy animal, provided the supplier has passed one audit and keeps transport temperature records and health certificates

questions.explanation: Paragraph 1.5 requires that only animals housed and bred for this purpose in a barrier facility be used, and that wild animals or abattoir sources must in no case be used; tissues from founder animals are likewise not to be used.

questions.question: A company manufactures a medicinal product fractionated from human plasma. According to the Scope of Annex 2B, which Annex should be consulted?

options.A: Annex 2A, because plasma-derived products are a type of ATMP
options.B: Annex 7, because plasma is a human-derived non-transgenic starting material
options.C: Annex 12, because all plasma products must be virally inactivated by irradiation
options.D: Annex 14, as medicinal products derived from the fractionation of blood or plasma have their own dedicated guidance

questions.explanation: The Scope of Annex 2B states that medicinal products derived from the fractionation of human blood or plasma are covered by Annex 14, while non-transgenic plant products are covered by Annex 7.

questions.question: When starting and raw materials need to be sterilised, what are the preferred method and the other available methods according to Annex 2B, paragraph 34?

options.A: Irradiation is preferred, with heat or filtration used only when necessary, to avoid heat degradation of the material
options.B: Heat wherever possible, with other methods such as irradiation and filtration also usable when necessary
options.C: Filtration is preferred, with heat or chemical sterilants used only when necessary, to reduce cost
options.D: Heat always, with irradiation or filtration not permitted, to avoid residue risks and material degradation

questions.explanation: Paragraph 34 states that sterilisation should be carried out by heat wherever possible, and that other suitable methods such as irradiation and filtration may be used when necessary. The option of always using heat misreads "preferred" as "the only method", while the options preferring irradiation or filtration reverse the order of preference.

questions.question: Chromatography equipment is used in a multi-product or campaign manufacturing environment. What is the attitude of the text in Annex 2B, paragraph 59, towards using the same chromatography matrix?

options.A: Re-use of the same matrix at different stages is discouraged, and the column lifetime must be defined
options.B: Re-use of the same matrix at different stages is encouraged, to reduce cost and batch-to-batch variation
options.C: As long as it is regenerated after every batch, the same matrix may be used for different products without limit
options.D: Only the operating conditions of the matrix need to be defined, with no need to set a lifetime or a sterilisation method

questions.explanation: Paragraph 59 requires a control strategy to be established using QRM, discourages re-use of the same matrix at different processing stages, and requires acceptance criteria, operating conditions, regeneration methods, lifetime and sanitisation or sterilisation methods to be defined.

questions.topic: Entry of materials into clean areas
questions.question: In an aseptic process, a batch of heat stable material is to enter the clean area. According to Annex 2B, paragraph 50, what is the method of entry preferred in the text?

options.A: Through an air lock with interlocked doors, with an effective surface disinfection procedure
options.B: Irradiate the surface with a UV lamp on site, then carry it directly from the ordinary corridor into the clean area
options.C: Through a double-ended autoclave or oven into the clean area
options.D: Sterilise it outside the clean area and, in single-layer packaging, bring it in through the ordinary material flow route

questions.explanation: Paragraph 50 states that heat stable material should preferably enter through a double-ended autoclave or oven; an interlocked air lock combined with surface disinfection is the approach for heat labile materials.

questions.question: Where there are several strains of the same bacterial species, or very similar viruses, and a spillage occurs, how may the validation of the decontamination procedure be simplified according to Annex 2B, paragraph 55?

options.A: Every strain must be validated separately, and the results for other strains may not be used instead
options.B: Only the least virulent strain needs to be validated, and all the other strains are regarded as covered
options.C: Validation need only be done once and applies permanently, regardless of differences in resistance to the agent between strains
options.D: One representative strain can be used for validation, unless there is reason to believe that the strains differ significantly in resistance

questions.explanation: Paragraph 55 allows validation with one representative strain, but this simplification cannot be used if there is reason to believe that different strains differ significantly in their resistance to the agent.
